test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 July 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A cylindrical rod of iron, whose height is equal to the radius of its base, is melted and cast into spherical balls, each of whose radius is half the radius of the base of the rod. Find the number of spherical balls thus made.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **radius** of the **cylindrical rod** be r. Then **height** h = r.

**Radius** of each **spherical ball** = r/2.

Number of balls = Volume of Cylinder ÷ Volume of 1 Sphere

Number of balls = (π × r² × r) ÷ (4/3 × π × (r/2)³) = r³ ÷ (4/3 × r³/8) = 1 ÷ (1/6) = 6.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 balls.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

For **Cylindrical Rod**: Radius = R, Height (H) = R.

For **Spherical Ball**: Radius (r) = R/2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ea5cc8c49621e1db2e17b128e0f21b017c4f21c68aabe776d040c86f4758fda.png] 

**Formula used:**

**Volume of Cylinder** = πR²H

**Volume of Sphere** = (4/3)πr³

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of **Iron Rod** = π × R² × R = πR³

⇒ Volume of one **Spherical Ball** = (4/3) × π × (R/2)³

⇒ Volume of one **Spherical Ball** = (4/3) × π × (R³/8) = πR³/6

⇒ Number of balls (n) = Volume of Rod ÷ Volume of Ball

⇒ n = πR³ ÷ (πR³/6)

⇒ n = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 balls.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a 3D solid is **melted** and recast into new shapes, the **total volume** remains constant.

Cylinder Properties

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh; Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h).

Sphere Properties

Surface Area = 4πr². For a **hemisphere**, Volume = (2/3)πr³ and Total Surface Area = 3πr².</p
